notes: The head of נֹפֶת is a genuine choice between droppings and honeycomb; the subtraction test was taken to leave droppings as the lexeme-bearing word, the competing reading being that the ASV elsewhere writes honeycomb alone.

Reading מָתוֹק as an attributive inside a nominal expression would keep which with the adjective; the parallel colon's כִּי־טוֹב → for it is good shows a predication of the same shape rendered as a main clause, so rule 41's limit governs and the relative is added.
